design_lock.frontage_rule: one continuous black steel canopy with cedar soffit
design_lock.opening_rule: physical transparent storefronts with occupied modeled depth

research.title: Lower East Side Retail Storefront
research.lesson: A continuous canopy can unify distinct ground-floor tenants while acting as a clear facade datum.

research.title: Strip Mall Maestro
research.lesson: Careful material continuity, recessed door rhythm, signage visibility and screened service functions can turn ordinary retail typology into coherent architecture.

research.title: Supreme Store / Neil Logan Architect
research.lesson: A deep horizontal storefront incision in brick makes glazing read as constructed depth rather than a surface graphic.

sources.prompt_summary: Photoreal 60 m contemporary prairie retail strip with one raised left brick anchor, six smaller tenant bays, continuous black-and-cedar canopy, transparent occupied storefronts and integrated right restaurant patio.
Straight-on architectural elevation preserving exact massing, seven-bay rhythm, sign panels, canopy and occupied glazing.
High-oblique roof view with pale membrane, exactly seven HVAC units, two restaurant exhausts, roof curbs, drains, scuppers and complete canopy.
Rear-right service elevation with seven aligned service zones, doors, meter banks, lights, drains and one screened two-bin enclosure.
Two-bay close-up locking low-E glass, thermally broken frames, recessed entrances, door hardware, brick mortar, cedar soffit and occupied retail depth.
Integrated right corner restaurant with wrapped glazing, aligned timber pergola, black rail, tables, planters and occupied interior.
Orthographic 3x2 plate of russet brick, charcoal micro-ribbed metal, cedar soffit, low-E storefront, concrete and roof membrane.
